articleTitle: A class D switching power amplifier with high efficiency and wide bandwidth by dual feedback loops
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The pulse width modulated class D power amplifier has the highest efficiency among various classes of amplifiers. However the performances, such as bandwidth, distortion and stability are inferior to those of the conventional class A or B. This paper presents a new class D amplifier employing dual feedback loops, namely current and voltage feedback considering complex impedances of the loudspeakers. The novel class D amplifier provides wide full-power bandwidth and stability at any load with high efficiency.

articleTitle: MPEG compliance bitstream design
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A method is described for designing bitstreams that can be used to test MPEG decoders without requiring prior knowledge of the particular circuit implementation. Visual inspection of the video output is used to evaluate the tests.

articleTitle: IC for motion-compensated 100 Hz TV with smooth-motion movie-mode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An IC for consumer 100 Hz television is presented. It applies motion estimation and compensation techniques for very high-quality field rate up-conversion and a judder-free motion portrayal of movie material. The IC is fabricated with an 0.8 /spl mu/m CMOS process.

articleTitle: INFLUENCE OF RF OSCILLATORS ON AN OFDM SIGNAL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: STORAGE AND RETRIEVAL OF COMPRESSED IMAGES
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Optimal variable quantization for JPEG extensions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present optimal variable quantization techniques for the newly proposed JPEG extensions from ISO/IEC 10918-3 (ITU-T Recommendation T.84). Variable quantization for each block is necessary to transcode from any video compression format (e.g. MPEG). It also gives increased subjective quality and efficient utilization of the channel bandwidth. The selective refinement extension is useful for selecting a part of an image for further refinement. In our experiments, we compare the reconstructed image obtained by variable quantization to that of the JPEG baseline system.

articleTitle: Single chip processor for CDP and CDROM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a single chip for compact disc players (CDPs) including the digital servo, DSP and 1 bit DAC. In the digital servo (by using the AGC function, and a new jump algorithm and auto adjust) it has eliminated manual adjust points and obtained high reliability, In the DSP part (by using the digital PLL) it needs no adjustable points, and increased the stability and reduced the locking time, and by using the 1 bit DAC it increased the audio performance and resolution for digital volume control. By integrating the three parts in a single chip, it reduced the set PCB area.

articleTitle: High performance integrated video decoder for multimedia video applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a high performance integrated video decoder which converts analog video signals to various video data, e.g., RGB, CCIR601, and square pixel video data, for more flexible multimedia video applications. Its performance has been proved after evaluation. A combing technique to reduce dot crawl noise caused by cross-luminance noise has been newly applied in the multimedia video interface area. Its effectiveness was proved by greatly reducing the noise effect on display monitors.

articleTitle: Automatic cut and camera operation detection for video
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Video should be segmented into shots to be used for identification and indexing. Various changes may happen within a single shot such as those related to camera operations, object movements, flashes, etc. Various similarities between different shots may also occur. Therefore, techniques based on interframe comparisons may result in detecting false cuts or missing true cuts if the appropriate threshold has not been chosen. In this paper, we propose a detection algorithm that understands and detects various changes within a shot in order to detect the cuts between separate shots.

articleTitle: Channel models for comparison of OFDM-, VSB-, QAM-modulation for digital terrestrial TV transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Based on computer generated channel models the performance of OFDM-, VSB and QAM-modulation for digital terrestrial broadcast TV transmission are compared. The main problem to be solved is the test under identical conditions of the different modulation schemes with a suitable software environment capable of simulating the properties of the channel and the modulations as closely as possible. Much of the paper is intended to provide an introductory review of the used transmission schemes and channel models, and how they are used in analysis. The multipath parts of our models rely for a great deal on the COST 207 multipath channel models.

articleTitle: DEVELOPMENT OF HIGH-BRIGHTNESS COMPACT LC PROJECTOR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Eigentransforms for region-based image processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Linear transforms such as the DCT are efficient for image compression. While known transforms that approximate the eigentransform are limited to rectangular regions, this paper proposes a model for construction of eigentransforms for arbitrarily-shaped image segments.

articleTitle: 64/256 QAM chip-set for digital CATV application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A small and cost effective 16/32/64/256 QAM receiver chip-set is developed for next generation digital CATV systems. The QAM receiver was partitioned into a two-chip set, analog and digital chip for board size reduction. Most of all the analog parts except the tuner is incorporated in one chip. The digital adaptive equalizer with about 470 k-transistors has been implemented on a 35 mm/sup 2/ die using a 0.5 /spl mu/m CMOS technology and with an optimized filter circuit.

articleTitle: TV AND TVSAT MIXER - OSCILLATOR PLL ICs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF AC-3 CODERS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: EMBEDDABLE CMOS 3.3V ANALOG FRONT END FOR CD APPLICATIONS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Ultra fast synchronized symbol timing recovery
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In personal communication systems the burst mode data transmission being more widely used, like in digital cellular phone, cellular digital packet data, Mobitex, and DECT. An ultra fast synchronized symbol timing recovery approach is presented. It is based on the balanced threshold zero crossing differential phase evaluation of the input baseband signal, and instantly locks the phase of a numerical controlled oscillator. This symbol timing recovery is implemented by a digital circuit. Measurement shows that in the burst mode data transmission, within 3 bits it can extract the timing clock from the input signal, with very little degradation in BER performance and jitter acquaintance.

articleTitle: A low power MPEG-2 decoder chip-set for set-top box
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An extremely low power MPEG-2 decoder chipset, requiring only +3.3 volt power supply, has been developed. We have designed the chip-set with various functionalities to be easily integrated into set-top boxes and other digital applications.

articleTitle: A Viterbi, convolutional interleave, and Reed-Solomon decoder IC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A single IC performs a concatenated forward error correction and conforms to the European digital video broadcast (DVB) specification. The key parameters of the codes are programmable and each function can be individually enabled allowing the IC to be applied to a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: The impact of display parameters on the quality perceived by the viewers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An investigation, based on subjective tests according to ITU Recommendation 500, was carried out to correlate the TV contrast-definition parameters to the subjective quality perceived by the viewers. The results show that high definition pictures (HDTV) with reduced contrast have a subjective quality comparable to that of pictures with standard definition (SDTV) and high contrast. Tests were carried out at the HDTV design viewing distance: 3 times the screen height (DVD=3H). A test using the preferred viewing distance (PVD) was also carried out. The PVD is a subjective parameter, a function of the screen height. For the 38", HDTV, 16/9 screen used in this test, the PVD was 5.2H. The results show that the design of new displays for HDTV should guarantee large screen with adequate contrast in order that the higher definition contribution not be made useless.

articleTitle: A QAM demodulation concept for digital video cable transmission
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: For the reception of digital video via cable systems, Philips Semiconductors has developed a concept for demodulating 4, 16, 32, and 64 QAM signals as well as conventional multistandard terrestrial video signals. The basic functions are the tuner, IF front-end QAM demodulation and forward error correction. This concept interfaces easily with the Philips Semiconductors source decoding concept.

articleTitle: A HIGHLY INTEGRATED PROCESSOR FOR IMPROVED QUALITY TELEVISION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: One-chip digital signal processor for ANC (active noise control) applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: One-chip digital signal processor has been developed, which is suitable for active noise control (ANC). This chip includes dual 8-bit ADCs, a DAC, CMOS operational amplifiers, a 16 bit fixed point arithmetic DSP and a 2K-ROM. It is fabricated using 0.8 /spl mu/m double poly, double metal CMOS process.

articleTitle: A 10-bit ADC (3 V, 50 mW, 20 Msamples/s) for camcorder applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a 10-bit, 20 Msamples/s ADC with a 3 V supply. It has been implemented using the folding and interpolation technique and is optimized for low current consumption. The chip is fabricated with a BiCMOS process and occupies 7 mm/sup 2/ of silicon.

articleTitle: Digital ultrafast carrier recovery for interactive transmission systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An ultrafast, all-digital method for phase synchronization and coherent carrier recovery is proposed for time division multiple access (TDMA) and code division multiple access (CDMA) burst data communication systems. In interactive transmission systems using burst data communications, instantaneous phase acquisition is crucial to properly demodulate the data and reduce the amount of preamble overhead bits. The new adaptive phase tracking (APT) method proposed, uses a hard-limited IF signal in a feed forward configuration for carrier phase detection and recovery. It is shown experimentally that this method is quite robust with respect to acquisition time and bit error rate (BER) performance for a binary phase shift keyed (BPSK) signal. A low power, low cost single chip fast carrier synchronization and demodulation solution for QPSK, GMSK and GSM compatible OQPSK and Feher's quadrature phase shift keyed (FQPSK) and binary phase shift keyed (FBPSK) systems are also presented.

articleTitle: Designing a set-top box operating system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Presents a discussion of the issues involved in the design of an operating system for an interactive television set-top box. Conventional operating system inadequacies and necessary set-top box extensions are discussed. Our operating system is cited as an example.

articleTitle: A 10-BIT 70MHz 3.3V CMOS 0.5/spl mu/m D/A CONVERTER FOR VIDEO APPLICATIONS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Development of a wide TV system equipped with 2/3 vertical expansion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new TV system equipped with a digital filter which expands a given 4:3 image vertically at the rate of 2/3 to fit into a 16:9 wide monitor leading to a pleasing visual quality. The algorithm for enlarging an image vertically can be classified in two categories: deflection and digital signal processing. The digital signal processing scheme is employed to overcome the shortcomings introduced by the deflection scheme, and it maintains the resolution of the image with a good quality.

articleTitle: One chip 2fH up-converter for high end/HDTV TV receivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Presents a description of a one-chip up-converter architecture study, which performs a 1fH to 2fH, line-doubling, video up-conversion, for both 50 Hz-625 lines and 60 Hz-525 lines video systems. This architecture concept, the DMU (dual mode up-converter), converts the interlaced digital YUV video input signals into either a non-interlaced progressive 1 V field rate (50 Hz/60 Hz) or a interlaced doubled 2 V field rate (100 Hz/120 Hz) display format.

articleTitle: A Micro Miniaturized CCD Color Camera Utilizing A Newly Developed CCD Packaging Technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A Force Feedback Joystick and Its Use in PC Video Games
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Active periodic noise control using a single FPGA chip
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) offer a quick and cost effective implementation for medium to large size digital designs that traditionally have been carried out by ASIC or DSPs. We present a simple design for an active periodic noise control system using only one FPGA. Experimental results show that with proper adjustment of the acoustic delay substantial noise reduction is achieved.

articleTitle: IEEE 1394 High Performance Serial Bus: The Digital Interface for ATV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A 1/4-INCH 380k-PIXEL IT-CCD IMAGE SENSOR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A tree structured wavelet transform coding scheme for digital HD-VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A wavelet transform coding method that fulfils the requirements of HD-VCR for studio applications is proposed. The algorithm exploits tree structure to represent the transformed coefficients and 2 level coder to achieve constant bit rate.

articleTitle: A Cost Effective Motion Estimation Processor LSI Using a Simple and Efficient Algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of MPEG-2 video coding for ATV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We examine the subjective and the objective performance of MPEG-2 main profile/high level for HDTV. Formal subjective assessment was performed by non-expert viewers on the sequences coded at a bit rate of 18 Mbits/s. Since MPEG-2 allows a great flexibility at the encoding end, we also examined the impact of various MPEG-2 encoding parameters on the quality of the reconstructed HDTV video sequences in terms of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: QAM FOR TERRESTRIAL AND CABLE TRANSMISSION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Grand Alliance transport stream demultiplexer design and implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The paper describes the Grand Alliance transport stream demultiplexer used for FCC testing. This prototype transport stream demultiplexer is responsible for processing a Grand Alliance transport stream, which is a constrained subset of the MPEG2 Systems Transport. The demultiplexer is of interest for HDTV receivers.

articleTitle: Development of a 21-inch a-Si TFT-LCD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The world largest display size (21-inch diagonal) full-color a-Si TFT-LCD has been developed. The key technologies and performances required to realize large area direct-view TFT-LCDs are discussed.

articleTitle: A format conversion algorithm based on sigmoid interpolation for HDTV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a simple but efficient 2-D format conversion algorithm for an HDTV system, where various source formats are allowed, based on an interpolation scheme which is referred to as a sigmoid interpolation. Illustrations are included showing the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm through a computer simulation.

articleTitle: IMPULSE NOISE CORRECTION IN TV TRANSMISSION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: DYNAMIC RANGE EXPANSION OF VIDEO CAMERAS BY ADAPTIVE GAMMA PROCESSING
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: New approach for mixing the RGB and CCIR601 formatted video signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new approach for digitally mixing the RGB and CCIR601 formatted video signals is proposed and realized using a 0.8 /spl mu/m CMOS process. Since mixing is performed digitally, more features are also added to the basic encoding function for more flexible multimedia applications. They are window keying, chroma keying, linear blending, and certain combinations of them.

articleTitle: An Active-Node Fault Diagnosis System for CEBus Networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: IMPLEMENTATION OF A PASSIVE AUTOMATIC FOCUSING ALGORITHM FOR DIGITAL STILL CAMERA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A new algorithm for active cancellation of fan noise
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A filtered-x least mean fourth algorithm is proposed which improves the convergence rate or reduces residual errors in noise cancellation systems.

articleTitle: A CONSUMER DIGITAL VCR FOR DIGITAL BROADCASTING
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An Experimental Digital Consumer Recorder for MPEG-coded Video Signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: PRE-PROCESSING FOR MPEG COMPRESSION USING ADAPTIVE SPATIAL FILTERING
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing: A Multi-Carrier Modulation Scheme
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Adaptive subsampling JPEG image coding
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present a JPEG-based image coding system which preprocesses the image by adaptive subsampling based on the local activity levels. As a result, it yields good quality in both smooth and complex areas of the image at high compression ratios. We propose an algorithm aiming at the improvement of the image quality at higher compression ratios than that JPEG can handle. This scheme combines decimation/interpolation and activity classification as the pre-/post-processing, and uses JPEG with optimal Q-tables as the compression engine. It yields better image quality than the original JPEG or the uniform subsampling JPEG. The increased complexity is only minor compared to JPEG itself.

articleTitle: Design of a Video Storage System for Interactive Video-on-Demand
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Multisync liquid crystal projector
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes an optical system with polarized beam splitter and a digitally controlled video signal processor, to achieve both high brightness and good uniformity of pictures, for liquid crystal display (LCD) projector, newly developed for multimedia presentation applications.

articleTitle: Multimedia applications and their bandwidth needs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Multimedia applications range from voice telephony to video on demand. Each application has very different bandwidth, switching, and traffic needs. This paper reviews typical cable TV architectures and basic communications system block diagrams. It defines the applications and explores the bandwidth resources needed to support a mix of these multimedia applications.

articleTitle: A single chip MPEG-1/CDROM decoder for video CD player applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Since the adoption of the white book (video CD) specification, the video CD player consumer market is becoming a reality. Players and titles are already available and market analysts predict a rapid growth, especially in Asia. This paper describes a device which allows a low cost consumer video CD player to be built.

articleTitle: Single-chip TV noise reduction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This new noise reduction IC for consumer TV automatically adapts to the noise level, and achieves 3 dB improvement when used stand-alone. It doubles the gain of current NR designs when cascaded.

articleTitle: VSB Modem Subsystem Design for Grand Alliance Digital Television Receivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A human-machine-interface design support tool for telecommunication terminal devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A human-machine-interface design support tool for telecommunication terminal devices was created. The computer-based tool rapidly constructs operation panels of target products based upon the function specifications of the products provided by the designers.

articleTitle: Point and pick user interface for projection television
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A point and pick graphical user interface has been developed for television. Bit-mapped menus are operated with a wireless pointer. Television and external component control has been consolidated into one button on a single remote control.

articleTitle: COMPUTATIONAL RAM IMPLEMENTATION OF AN ADAPTIVE VECTOR QUANTIZATION ALGORITHM FOR VIDEO COMPRESSION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: 3-CCD video camera system for consumer use
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new signal processing system for 3-CCD video cameras. This system provides as high quality images as systems for professional use, with compact hardware available for a palm corder for consumer use.

articleTitle: 4CCD COMPACT, LIGHT-WEIGHT, CONSUMER USE HDTV CAMERA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Color printer correction system by using fuzzy tree approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A fuzzy tree approach is proposed to solve the color correction problems between a scanner and a printer. Experimental results show that this methodology produces a good correction performance and has a low computational complexity.

articleTitle: A base band processing IC for analogue cordless telephones
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have designed an audio and data processing circuit for cordless telephone that contains a scrambler, a modem, and amplifiers for the microphone and receiver. The circuit can be fabricated into a single chip IC. The newly developed baseband signal processor is divided into two: an analog block made from a bipolar process and a digital block made from a CMOS process. The whole block can be fabricated using BiCMOS process technology.

articleTitle: The Grand Alliance HDTV video encoder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Members of the digital HDTV Grand Alliance have jointly designed and constructed an MPEG-2 main profile, high level video encoder as part of an overall HDTV broadcast system. The encoder accepts video in either the 1080 line (30 Hz) interlaced format or the 720 line (60 Hz) progressive format, and produces an MPEG-2 MP@HL compliant bitstream. The encoder processing includes large-area motion estimation, adaptive telecine processing, and an advanced rate control mechanism. This paper describes the hardware architecture and trade-offs of this encoder.

articleTitle: Hardware for image alignment by one shear transformation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a hardware for image alignment in an OCR system. This hardware uses a new image-aligning algorithm which performs one shear transformation with no losing pixel information when compared with traditional aligning algorithms. One shear transformation is performed by simply shifting pixels into the target area along a base line without computing new positions of all pixels for aligning. The effectiveness of this algorithm is demonstrated by aligning algorithms. In the hardware, a misaligned image made up of 480 by 380 pixels is aligned within 65 ms.

articleTitle: Video CCD based portable digital still camera
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Considerations for System Development of One-chip video MUSE(HDTV) decoder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: DESIGN AND EXPERIMENTAL EVALUATION OF A PILOT TONE AIDED CARRIER RECOVERY SYSTEM FOR WIRELESS PERSON
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: FUZZY LOGIC BASED IMAGE PROCESSING IN IQTV ENVIRONMENT
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: 218 MHz radio transceiver for IVDS spectrum
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a highly integrated packet data radio that operates in the 218-219 MHz interactive video and data services (IVDS) spectrum. The system and network architectures of this subscriber unit radio have been designed for low cost production.

articleTitle: A CAR-USE MINI DISC (MD) CHANGER
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: HD-SAT modems for the satellite broadcasting in the 20 GHz frequency band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present two satellite modems developed in the frame work of the European RACE II HD-SAT project. We describe the HD-SAT system by presenting briefly the overall system. The propagation conditions in the 20 GHz range are particularly detailed as well as the technical answer: the graceful degradation concept. We deal with the variable bit rate-TCM 8PSK modem. The features of this modem, mainly the variable bit rate possibilities between 85 and 70 Mb/s, are described. We describe the "graceful degradation" modem which uses a hierarchical modulation scheme with time multiplexed modulation.

articleTitle: GHOST CANCELLATION IMPLEMENTATION IN TELEVISION AND VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: SKIP PLAY TECHNOLOGY FOR HOME-USE DIGITAL VCRs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A STUDY OF THE RECORDING AND REPRODUCING SYSTEM OF DIGITAL VCR USING METAL EVAPORATED TAPE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Near-transparent audio coding at low bit-rate based on minimum noise loudness criterion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A low bit-rate audio coding method based on minimum noise loudness criterion of a psychoacoustic model is proposed. The lower bound of the bit rate versus the suggested perceptual distortion is also discussed. The problem encountered in processing wideband audio signal is its high bit-rate in limited bandwidth channel and high capacity requirement in storage media. Most of high quality audio compression methods heavily rely on human perception, or more precisely on simultaneous masking, to reduce the bit rate. In order to make an explicit and separate control to encode different frequency regions in the auditory spectrum, many compression methods for wideband audio are based on spectral decomposition via linear transform or subband coding. A transform coder based on the human auditory model is designed.

articleTitle: MULTIGHOST CANCELLATION TECHNIQUE FOR HDTV SYSTEMS, USING A DERIVATION OF THE OLS LEARNING ALGORITHM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: NEW FEEDBACK VITERBI DECODER FOR DIGITAL VCRS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: EFMPlus: The Coding Format of the High-Density Compact Disc
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Advanced television captioning
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Work is continuing within the Television Data Systems Subcommittee (TDSS) of the Electronic Industries Association (EIA) to develop a closed-captioning system for inclusion into an advanced television signal. The working group's efforts are partially funded by the US Department of Education and the EIA. This paper provides a background of the work and a status of the progress. The goals of the Working Group include designing the overall architecture of the ATV captioning system, establishing the features, its display protocol, and the instruction set of computer commands which will trigger each display feature.

articleTitle: DEMULTIPLEXER IC FOR MPEG2 TRANSPORT STREAMS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: On variable bit rate video coding and multiplexing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A VBR (variable bit rate) video coding and multiplexing algorithm for DSM (digital storage media) application is described in the MPEG compliant manner. The BFOS (Breiman, Friedman, Olshen and Stone) algorithm is used for optimal bit allocation and VBR encoding under this bit allocation is introduced. Our VBR encoding provides more consistent picture quality in the MSE sense and better worst-case subjective-quality.

articleTitle: A COMMON CONDITIONAL ACCESS INTERFACE FOR DIGITAL VIDEO BROADCASTING DECODERS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Home Network Controller: A Cost-Effective Method for Providing Broadband Access to Residential Subsc
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: "Real channel" modem CAD system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given. The functionality and capability of a modem CAD environment that uses real channel impairments as test vectors is described. Examples of architecture that perform well in impaired transmission systems are presented.

articleTitle: ERROR CORRECTION SCHEMES FOR DIGITAL TELEVISION BROADCASTING
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: In-loop coring: robust MPEG coding for noisy images
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Predictive coding systems work best when the current image is easily predicted from other images. But when the source image contains noise, accurate prediction becomes difficult and as a result either the bit rate rises, picture quality drops, or both. Existing techniques for improving the quality of noisy source material coded with MPEG coders usually involve reducing the noise of the source material before presenting the video to the image coding system. Many techniques exist for reducing noise, and any or several of these may be brought to bear on the problem.

articleTitle: REWRITABLE DIGITAL VIDEO DISC SYSYTEM USING MAGNETO-OPTICAL DISC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A Multi-Layer Video Browsing System
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: The Heart of the New Information Appliance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A DIGITAL FM SIGNAL PROCESSING SYSTEM FOR VCRs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: On constant luminance, gamma correction, and digitization of color space
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: With one exception all color television standards, including proposed HDTV standards, violate the constant luminance principle by companding the RGB primaries. True luminance information is processed in the chroma channels. Visible luminance errors caused by processing and impairments in the chroma channels are reviewed and quantitatively analyzed. There is now a window of opportunity to develop digital TV standards without this well known flaw in TV color encoding. Digitization of color space and constant luminance proposals, including transmission of chromaticities, are examined. Further work leading to a constant luminance MPEG option, besides the linear option, is recommended.

articleTitle: A concept for source decoding in digital video broadcast applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: ICs for a full-featured "plug and play" MPEG2 digital video broadcast (DVB) source decoder for implementation in DVB integrated receiver decoders (IRDs) are presented. The ICs perform descrambling, demultiplexing, audio decompression, video decompression, composite video encoding as well as external interfacing. In addition to microcontroller-related memory, the source decoder requires only 16 Mbits of decompression memory. Only a minimum of peripheral hardware is required. Driver software support requirements are moderate. A microcontroller is only required to handle conditional access information, program specific information, and audio/video synchronization.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Raster Engine for Video Game, Multimedia PC and Interactive TV
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Development of an MPEG2 Decoder for Magneto - Optical Disk Video Players
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A decoder circuit has been developed which reads out and decompresses high-definition video images recorded on the magneto-optical disk by MPEG2 compression.

articleTitle: A 3.3 V 6 BITS 60 MHZ CMOS DUAL ADC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: All bipolar 3V 20 mW tracking servo LSI for 8 MM VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Using only bipolar technology, we have developed the first 3 V tracking servo LSI for 8 mm VCR. This LSI has succeeded in realizing lower cost, drastically reducing power consumption, and eliminating digital blocks.

articleTitle: Multimedia capabilities of long distance networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Multimedia communication is available now and for many applications is cost effective at existing tariffs. There is sufficient but not excess bandwidth available in long distance networks. The growth of multimedia dialog communication is restricted to users with compatible terminal systems.

articleTitle: Measurement of television direct pickup (DPU) in a GTEM cell
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The requirements of the new cable bill specify the amount of signal a television tuner may receive over the air, this is known as direct pickup (DPU). DPU is readily definable in terms of antenna parameters. The theoretical basis and measurement technique used to quantify the DPU of a television tuner using a GTEM is examined.

articleTitle: An ISDN basic rate interface videophone with a multipoint communicating function
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An economical multipoint audiovisual communicating system technology for the ISDN basic rate interface is introduced. The system offers multipoint audiovisual communication using the ring-type connection via the two B channels in the ISDN basic rate interface for each terminal. The system's connection control offers a terminal skipping procedure. Multipoint image processing produces a divided display by digital data manipulation. Finally, an ISDN basic rate interface videophone using this system technology is described.

articleTitle: DIGITAL GEOMETRY CORRECTION AND DEFLECTION CONTROL SYSTEM FOR MULTI-SCAN MONITORS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Revised record/playback interface systems for GA-HDTV, HD-VCR and D3 VTR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes revised versions of the three recording/playing back interface systems. Modifications were required to meet the current HDTV transport data formats which were significantly changed in accordance with the Grand Alliance (GA) specification. The first interface is for recording the compressed data from the GA-HDTV transmitter to D3 digital VTR, the second is for the GA-HDTV receiver to the HD-VCR and the third is for the HD-VCR to D3 VTR. The interface hardware was fully developed and tested in preparing for the GA-HDTV systems laboratory testing in April, 1995 at ATTC and field testing in Charlotte, North Carolina.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of VCR servo system via discrete and nonlinear methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, the stability analysis of a VCR servo system is developed in the discrete time domain with nonlinear analysis of the limiter effect. As a result, we can find rigorous stability criteria that were not known by the conventional linear continuous approximation method. In addition, gain tuning methods that can assure stable operations of servo system are also presented.

articleTitle: Residential customer premises equipment in a telecommuting application
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: To illustrate the issues surrounding multimedia in the home, we choose a telecommuting application as being representative of the issues. Telecommuting is becoming a more popular option for companies who have to reduce commuting loss and for those who have limited office space. In this application a worker at home is connected with his office by video, audio, and by a computer network. Telephone and fax communication is usually included in the requirements. An illustration of the components of a video conferencing home set-up is included.

articleTitle: A monolithic deflection controller for autosync monitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a new deflection controller IC for monitors. It has full horizontal and vertical autosync capability and offers a comprehensive set of functions for raster correction, protection, and SMPS control. As an outstanding feature, the IC utilizes automatic tracking between the external adjustments for picture size, picture position and raster correction. This combination of high integration level and well defined module interactions simplifies the design of modern autosync monitors.

articleTitle: An approach from cognitive science and semiotics for evaluating and designing user interface of audio-visual products
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An evaluation and design method for improving user interfaces concerning audio-visual products is proposed, developed by systemizing cognitive science achievements through a semiotic approach. The usefulness of this approach in product development is also discussed.

articleTitle: A Mandarin speech autodialer with adaptation ability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A Mandarin speech autodialer using unit of diphthong and Bayesian reference models is presented. Besides, an effective speaker adaptation technique based on the generalized probabilistic descent algorithm is developed and integrated into the speech autodialer system. Experimental results show that a good performance is obtained.

articleTitle: Hybrid video sequence coder using fractals
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A hybrid image compression scheme which combines the resolution advantage of fractal image compression and the computational simplicity of motion vector compensation method, is presented. The optimum block sizes and quantization are determined and performance factors are evaluated by experimenting with typical video conference image sequences. The scheme can provide a compression ratio up to 70 with such images while retaining excellent picture quality.

articleTitle: Digital decoder chipset for improved wide-screen TV receivers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Prototype PALplus TV sets used programmable signal processing devices to demonstrate the decoder functions. In preparation for larger-scale production of PALplus sets, a co-design/development activity has been initiated between Philips Semiconductors and Philips Sound and Vision to implement the decoder function in two application specific submicron CMOS ICs. The specification of these ICs satisfies the requirements of the PALplus system specification. Interfacing to the existing architecture of a digital feature environment is provided The chipset has a digital I/O allowing optimal picture quality for 100 Hz PALplus TV sets. Samples are expected in mid 1995 to meet the target for the introduction of PALplus TV sets using the dedicated chipset during the 1995 Internationale Funkausstellung (IFA).

articleTitle: Digital audio processor for consumer-use digital VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a digital audio processor for a digital VCR. This LSI can speedily control the external RAM, which accumulates the audio data to be delayed for synchronizing with the video data and shuffles them over tracks and data sync blocks within a frame. This LSI has achieved high quality sound and strong error recovery.

articleTitle: A study on the interchangeability of the center-rotating drum VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new method to measure tape motion on the helix guide of the drum was developed, by which real-time and highly precise observations were done. Thus the optimum mechanical conditions were decided and good track straightness was achieved.

articleTitle: FACE: familiarity in user interface for consumer products
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The FACE guidelines define a set of user interface (UI) design rules. The target of these rules is to increase the sense of familiarity between different consumer electronics products.

articleTitle: Software implementation of a real time color quantization for full-color video quality
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a new real-time color quantization method for realizing full-color video quality. The method utilizes a pseudo-color assignment table (PAT) that transforms the input video signals to optimal color-codes with dithering. We have confirmed that the PAT method has a higher speed and a better quality than those of previous methods. The PAT method is suitable for the implementation of personal computer software.

articleTitle: AN OPTICAL INTERFACE SYSTEM FOR CAMERA/RECORDER
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A core-based digital audio signal processor for Hi-Fi audio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A second-generation core DSP suited for digital audio applications has been developed. The first DASP (digital audio signal processor) with the core-DSP implements the dedicated audio, host, and external memory interfaces. The DSP, which is the central processing role in the Hi-Fi audio systems, has been specifically developed by many LSI manufacturers. The manufacturers in the consumer market always require low cost devices. This new DASP has been enhanced with many new functions, which are discussed.

articleTitle: An economical solution for video CD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A single chip, video CD decoder is described which has been optimized for low cost consumer video CD players complying with the current version (2.0) of the video-CD standard. A summary of decoder features is given with particular emphasis on the decoder features provided for support of video CD play control lists and "trick modes".

articleTitle: An optical pointer for infrared remote controllers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An infrared optical pointing system is described for interactive remote controllers to allow the positioning of a cursor on a TV screen. A simple lens and 4 quadrant photodetector in the remote controller are used to measure the angle of incidence of light received from an infrared reference beam.

articleTitle: A NEW RADIO RECEIVER SYSTEM FOR PERSONAL COMMUNICATIONS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A model-based facial image recognition method for image synthesizing system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper reports a new facial feature point extraction method for an image synthesizing system. The method works successfully with images of more than 1000 Japanese and 500 Americans. A sample of application is reported.

articleTitle: An Image Restoration System for a Single-CCD Color Camcorder
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Text segmentation for automatic document processing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: There has been a considerable interest in designing automatic systems that can scan a given paper document and store it on electronic media for easier storage, manipulation and access. Most documents contain graphics and images, in addition to text. Thus, the document image has to be segmented to identify text and image regions, so that appropriate techniques may be applied to those regions. We present a new technique for image segmentation in which text and image regions, in a given document image, are automatically identified. Technique is based on a differential-processing text extraction concept. The proposed technique is capable of analysing complex document image layouts. The document image is processed by using textural feature analysis. The results of the proposed method are presented with test images which demonstrate the robustness of the technique.

articleTitle: Development of aspect ratio conversion system using scan-line video processor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed an aspect ratio conversion (ARC) system using a scan-line video processor (SVP) for various types of NTSC signal; ARC algorithms were implemented by programming the SVP and an interlaced to progressive scan conversion (IPC) system was added using an ASIC chip.

articleTitle: Implementation of Low Power One-Chip MUSE(HDTV)Video Processor Using Consumer Oriented Macros
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Evolution of a remote control locator system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the development evolution of a remote control locator system for television. Although the locator system described is restricted in its scope to television, its application in other areas is readily apparent. The remote control locator functions as a closed-loop system. One aspect of the system operates via RF control; the other is IR (infrared).

articleTitle: Experiment Test and Evaluation of a GMSK chipset compatible with the GSM PCS standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: MPEG-2 VIDEO DECODER FOR THE DIGITAL HDTV GRAND ALLIANCE SYSTEM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Step-by-step towards the compatible SECAMplus system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Enhancing the SECAM system includes introducing of 16:9 aspect ratio, reducing of cross-color and cross-luminance disturbances, transmitting the helper and introducing stereo sound. A step by step improvement, making the SECAMplus system as close as possible to PALplus would facilitate its adoption and development of two-standard wide-screen TV sets.

articleTitle: A 7K-PIXEL X 3LINE COLOR LINEAR SENSOR WITH SINGLE-SIDED READOUT METHOD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Automatic white balance of digital still camera
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Progress of the National Data Broadcasting standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A National Data Broadcasting Committee (NDBC) has been formed in 1993 to develop a standard for broadcasting high speed digital data together with standard NTSC transmissions. These signals should not affect standard NTSC receivers but can be received and decoded by specially designed receivers. The NDBC received five proposals and two proponents submitted hardware for testing. The other proposals were withdrawn. The two systems which were tested were not similar in implementation and performance but generally demonstrated the capability of transmitting digital data together with the NTSC signal.

articleTitle: HDTV scan converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A hardware implementation of the video scan converter for a Grand Alliance high definition television (GA-HDTV) system is described.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Coding Scheme for HDTV Sequences
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Surface acoustic wave filters in digital television systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An overview of current SAW technologies and their application to digital terrestrial, cable, and satellite receiver systems is presented. SAW filters have long been used as TV IF filters, but digital transmission systems bring new application possibilities. Modelling techniques for high frequency design are described along with a discussion of important tradeoffs for use as a replacement or enhancement for baseband DSP functions.

articleTitle: Bayesian techniques for HDTV channel equalization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper applies Bayesian conditional decision feedback estimation (BCDFE) techniques to HDTV channel equalization. We propose a new blind equalization architecture which combines the BCDFE and conditional gradient algorithms to jointly estimate the transmitted data and channel parameters. The proposed structure performs smooth transitions between trained and blind operation, and can provide promising performance of equalization in HDTV fading channels.

articleTitle: The Development of Audio and Video Signal Processing LSI for SD-DVC
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: ADJUSTMENT-FREE LSI CHIP-SET FOR CD PLAYER APPLICATION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Embeddable CMOS 3.3 V 16 bits monobit and multibit delta-sigma digital to analog converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An embeddable 16 bits digital to analog oversampled converter was developed in 3.3 V, 0.5 /spl mu/m full CMOS technology. It uses a "131+46" or "27+7+5" taps anti-aliasing filter and a third order monobit or second order multibit delta-sigma modulator followed by a second order switch-capacitor filter. This cell was designed to be a part of audio products chips like CD or MPEG decoder systems.

articleTitle: Performance of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing system in terrestrial TV channels-a statistical analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, the performance of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) in terrestrial TV channels is investigated. Using a statistical channel model, the results will be derived semianalytically for OFDM systems. In this study, we give outage probability characteristics for terrestrial digital TV systems. We obtain results for two kinds of equalization methods and additionally for a system without equalization.

articleTitle: GHOST CANCELLING FOR MOBILE TELEVISION
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A new ECC LSI for consumer-use digital VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The newly developed ECC (error control coding) LSI for consumer-use digital VCR systems has two main functions. One is the encoding and decoding of error control codes, and the other is the packing and unpacking of audio/video/subcode/ID data. We propose a new ECC LSI that has clear functions and simple interfaces to other LSI sets and reduces its size by using a single RS(2/sup 8/) decoder.

articleTitle: New RF signal processor IC design for the Mini Disc system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new RF signal processor IC for the MD (Mini Disc) system. We developed an RF signal processor IC with higher performance, smaller size and lower power consumption. This chip contains an I/V amplifier, a RF amplifier, an ALPC (automatic laser power control), an ADIP (address in pregroove) demodulator, an FE low band amplifier and switch blocks all in one chip. The IC is fabricated using double metal 0.8 /spl mu/m BiCMOS technology.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis on Distribution of M-QAM HDTV Signals over FTTF Network
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Optimization techniques for high order phase-locked loop type jitter reduction circuit for digital audio
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Techniques like gain peaking reduction and the selection of voltage-controlled-crystal-oscillator (VCXO) frequency are addressed in this paper. The new gain peaking reduction criterion provides far better jitter attenuation when compared with that using maximum phase margin.

articleTitle: DEVELOPMENT OF HDTV DIGITAL TRANSMISSION SYSTEMI THROUGH SATELLITE
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An adaptive reduced-state sequence detector utilizing the symbol-aided method in the mobile satellite channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive RSSD receiver, which is a suboptimal alternative to the adaptive maximum likelihood detector and is able to track the time-varying ISI channels in the mobile satellite channel. The structure of the proposed adaptive RSSD is a modified RSSD utilizing a per-survivor processing as well as the symbol-aided method and a channel estimator using the tentative data sequences with a small decision delay. The complexity and performance of the proposed adaptive RSSD are controlled by the number of states and the inserting period of the known symbols. The simulation results show the fact that the proposed adaptive RSSD obtains excellent tracking performance over time-varying ISI channels.

articleTitle: MPEG1 and MPEG2 system layer implementation trade-off between micro coded and FSM architecture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In the context of digital consumer applications, it has been necessary to develop a parser handling the MPEG1 and MPEG2 system layer. This application is embedded either in the front end of audio, or video decoders, or as a back end of demultiplexer serving these applications. It works at 24 MHz and is implemented in 0.5 micron technology. Micro coded (MC) and finite state machine (FSM) architecture have been evaluated in detail, in order to manage trade-offs including flexibility, performance, development time, area versus timing or area versus scheduling.

articleTitle: A STUDY ON A HIGH DENSITY DIGITAL VIDEO DISC PLAYER
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: IMPEG-2 video encoder based on VLSI chip set
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A real-time MPEG-2 video encoder has been developed based on a set of four dedicated IC designs. The encoder compresses video pictures according to ITU-R 601 recommendation into bit streams from 1.15 Mbit/s to 15 Mbit/s according to the specifications of the MPEG-2 video standard, Main Profile at Main Level (MP@ML). Other input formats can be handled, including various HDTV source formats, which are converted into bit streams of the Main Profile at High Level.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Cutter for MPEG-1 System Streams
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A SINGLE CHIP MPEG1 DECODER
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Video Disc System Using Variable Bit Rate
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: "Browse search using audio key-information" for multimedia on-demand systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: "Browse search using audio key-information" enhances the information search on multimedia on-demand systems. In this scheme, audible digests (key-information), used for browsing, are provided synchronously with text based indexes to the corresponding information.

articleTitle: Data slicing and decoding technique in Videoinfo system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Videoinfo, a Chinese teletext system, is under development in Taiwan. One of the key technical issues in providing such teletext services is that data must be received by the receiving end promptly and correctly. This paper addresses the overall system architecture and the technique of data slicing and decoding in Videoinfo.

articleTitle: VSB MODULATION USED FOR TERRESTRIAL BROADCASTS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Analysis of the Grand Alliance HDTV transmission subsystem field test measurements in Charlotte, North Carolina
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given. In the spring of 1994, a prototype 8VSB transmission subsystem designed and built by the HDTV Grand Alliance was submitted for field trials in Charlotte, North Carolina. Tests were conducted employing both VHF channel 6 and UHF channel 53, and data were collected from approximately 200 receiving locations in and around Charlotte. The paper reports on the results and analysis of the measured data.

articleTitle: EXPERIMENTAL INVESTIGATION ON MPEG-2 BASED VIDEO CODING AT 22 Mbps
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Bridging Standards for Digital Television Broadcast
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Architecture design of MPEG-2 decoder system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An architecture for the VLSI design of an MPEG-2 video decoder is introduced to achieve the MP@ML (main profile, main level). The hardware complexity is analyzed, and the decoding unit is designed to reach the required performance. The decoding unit includes variable length decoding (VLD), inverse scan, inverse quantization (IQ), IDCT, and motion compensation.

articleTitle: MPEG2 3D PLAYER SYSTEM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: MPEG-2 DATA RATE RECORD ABLE 3.5 INCH OPTICAL DISK
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An Adjustment-Free LSI for the Video Signal Processing System
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Grand Alliance Prototype Transport Stream Encoder Design & Implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Double-pipelined 32-voice wavetable synthesizer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new double pipelined structure of wavetable synthesizer to simultaneously process 16-bit 32-voice for multimedia audio applications. The proposed synthesizer processes all the samples at a full 44.1 kHz rate, while almost all the wavetable systems being offered today operate at sampling rates ranging only from 22 to 32 kHz. This high performance structure has been realizes with a 0.8 /spl mu/m CMOS process.

articleTitle: Minimum Adjustment Analog Convergence System for Curved Faceplate Projection Tubes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A new tracking control system with playback RF signal for VCR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new tracking control system by mountain climbing method using playback RF signal was developed. In order to use the system without any conventional method, speed compensation control and dynamic mode control were developed. And a new detecting method of rotational phase for cylinder that also uses playback signal was developed.

articleTitle: Measuring system to analyze causes of VTR reproduced output fluctuation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed a method to quantitatively measure the VTR reproduced output fluctuation factors using two-frequency time division signals. It has been confirmed, that this method is effective in measuring off-track and spacing fluctuation separately, by a series of experiments.

articleTitle: Residential cable network requirements of interactive multimedia
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Today's modern cable systems already have some fiber mixed in with the coax, but they are still mainly one-way broadcast networks. In order to support the near term future needs of wideband, reliable two way networks; today's networks must evolve. This paper explores the nature of the evolution and the resulting hybrid fiber coax architectures.

articleTitle: A new video storage architecture for plasma display panels
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We deal with the necessity of a video storage unit for the AC-plasma display panel technology and its composition. After describing each function and its goal, we give a complete synopsis.

articleTitle: An on-line Chinese character recognition for personal communicator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An on-line Chinese character recognition (OLCCR) based all subword model for a personal communicator is presented. This OLCCR has three advantages such as short recognition time, high recognition rate and a small kernel memory size. The average rate of correct recognition is 99.1% within the top ten priorities of the recognition results. The average recognition time of one character is 0.415 second with the 486-33 personal computer. The occupied memory size of the program kernel, including the algorithm and template, is 480 Kbytes. The personal communicator would be intuitive and easy to use by combining it with the OLCCR that we developed.

articleTitle: ACCEPTABLE LIMITS OF GAMMA FOH A TFT-LIQUID CRYSTAL DISPLAY ON SUBJECTIVE EVALUATION OF PICTURE QUAL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: An 8-bit Y/C interface for digital video systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This Y/C interface includes complete multiple video sources analog circuitry and two 8-bit 32 MHz ADCs. Its power consumption of 0.5 W and low-noise architecture allows the use of a TQFP48 package.

articleTitle: A home multiple-function AV receiver/monitored control system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The paper presents the composition, function and features of the home multiple-function AV receiver/monitored control system. This system is composed of a camera, image motion detector, VTR, PC and multiple-function AV receiver/monitor with dual tuners TV, broadcast satellite reception and picture-in-picture (PIP).

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the oil-lubricated herringbone-grooved journal bearing for VCR drum assembly
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A numerical analysis is performed about the static and dynamic characteristics of the oil-lubricated herringbone bone-grooved journal bearing which has circular groove profile. Results are compared with the plain and herringbone-grooved journal bearing with rectangular groove profile.

articleTitle: AGC stability requirements for the decoder interface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In order to insure the RF AGC system is stable for any cable decoder connected to any receiver, the gain and time constants for both must be specified. These requirements and their development are given. The analysis results in a gain-bandwidth specification for the receiver's RF AGC line, a minimum phase response for both the receiver and decoder IF AGC loops, a maximum capacitance for the decoder AGC line and a minimum resistance for the receiver's AGC port. Further, the phase response for the IF AGC loops is separated into more easily measured gain and bandwidth requirements.

articleTitle: EDTV-II DECODER BY SVP2 (the 2nd generation of Scan-line Video Processor)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Putting usability into television
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes usability techniques used to ensure consumer centred design of a TV user interface. Key issues were the early involvement of usability experts, the complete process for making usable products, linking usability experts' work into normal consumer electronics product development, and finally assuring the usability of the completed product.

articleTitle: A multipurpose single chip JBIG based compression/decompression system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The Joint Bilevel Image Experts Group (JBIG) coding system was adopted as an international standard for next-generation image coding systems. An LSI which compresses/decompresses images 1-pixel/clock through pipeline architecture and conforms to JBIG and conventional modified Huffman/modified read/modified modified read (MH/MR/MMR) coding functions and has flexible bus configuration facilities to allow multipurpose use is described.

articleTitle: Camcorder low light sensitivity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The EIA (Electronic Industries Association) set up a group to study camcorder low light performance. This paper describes the work of the Camcorder Low Light Task Force and gives details of conditions to determine the low light sensitivity of consumer camcorders and video cameras.

articleTitle: REPEATER BETWEEN HOME SYSTEMS COAXIAL CABLE AND TWISTED PAIR MEDIA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: A MEDIUM RESOLUTION INTELLIGENT VIDEO CAMERA
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: RESPONSE IMPROVEMENT OF THE ACOUSTIC TRANSFER FUNCTION OF A HORN LOUDSPEAKER USING DIGITAL SIGNAL PR
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Proceedings of International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.
